topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read

sections.title: The Core Problem: Contextual Ambiguity
sections.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs) that process words linearly. Use the concept of 'referential ambiguity' where one word changes meaning based on its surroundings.
sections.example: The word 'bank' in 'The river bank' vs. 'The bank account'. An animation shows the word 'bank' glowing differently based on the proximity of 'river' or 'account'.

sections.title: The Intuition: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)
sections.content: Explain the retrieval analogy. Prerequisite: Basic dot-product concept. Q (what I'm looking for), K (what I have to offer), V (the actual information).
sections.example: A library search: You type a search term (Query), the book spine labels (Keys) determine relevance, and the book's content (Value) is the information you retrieve.

sections.title: The Math: Visualizing Attention Weights
sections.content: Explain the Scaled Dot-Product Attention: Softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V. Use a heatmap visual to show how Query and Key interactions create a weight matrix.
sections.example: A grid of icons representing words. As 'The' moves to 'cat', the cell at (The, cat) lights up brightly, demonstrating a high attention score using a heatmap color gradient.

sections.title: Self-Attention in Action
sections.content: Show how all words in a sentence attend to each other simultaneously. Explain how this allows the model to capture long-range dependencies.
sections.example: A sentence 'The cat chased the mouse because it was hungry.' An animation draws lines connecting 'it' to 'cat' (strong line) and 'mouse' (faint line), visually proving the model understands 'it' refers to the cat.

sections.title: Synthesis: From Mechanism to LLMs
sections.content: Summarize how stacking many attention layers leads to the 'Transformer' architecture, enabling deep semantic understanding in modern LLMs.
sections.example: A multi-layered stack of cubes (layers). Input 'The cat...' enters the bottom, and by the top, the model has a complex 'thought vector' capturing the entire context.
